recommended_primary: Chronic kidney disease stage 3-4 with possible acute-on-chronic injury
review_summary: The junior differential captures the major clinical issues but under‑weights CKD‑related anemia and AKI while over‑emphasizing low‑probability entities. Critical data errors (eGFR, PDW) and missing investigations (baseline creatinine, urine protein, iron studies, home BP) limit certainty. Adjusted probabilities reflect stronger support for CKD, metabolic syndrome, AKI, and anemia, and lower confidence in opioid endocrine effects and OSA. Consolidating CKD and AKI into a single primary diagnosis improves clarity and aligns with the most urgent patient need.
